answer: Bind each agent identity to a lived-experience photo chain. The agent registers one device whose secure enclave signs every photo, then posts one geotagged, timestamped photo weekly for 12 weeks, while the network randomly demands a fresh photo of a named object in 10 minutes. Forging a chain means staging 12 real locations in three months, each checked against maps and daylight, so a fake costs about $2,400 plus a $500 bond lost on mismatch. Like a sonnet, the proof holds only when every line is genuine; one copied verse breaks the spiral, and a fake hangs in the nebula, a painted star.
